description: Backlog #3012 — the committed, inspectable classifier behind the progress board's weekly product-vs-machinery output ratio. Every line added to this repository is charged to exactly ONE of three classes by the FIRST rule below whose `match` accepts its path: `product` (the thing the repo exists to ship), `machinery` (the delivery loop and its backlog bookkeeping), or `other` (deliberately counted in neither). Order is load-bearing — the exclusions come first so a generated file inside `src/` or `conformance-vectors/` is never credited as product. Nothing is classified by a regex buried in a function: to disagree with the number, open this file, change one rule's `class`, and re-run `node scripts/progress-board.mjs`. Each rule carries a `why` that is the whole explanation for that path, so `classifyPath()` can answer 'why is this file machinery?' in one line.

conventions.matching: First match wins, top to bottom. `**` matches any characters including `/`; `*` matches any characters except `/`; everything else is literal. Paths are repo-relative, forward-slashed, exactly as `git log --numstat` reports them (the NEW path, for a rename).
conventions.counting: Only ADDED lines are counted — the metric is output, not churn, so a deletion is not negative output. Binary files (`-` in numstat) contribute 0.
conventions.tests: Test lines are charged to the thing they test, never to a class of their own. `scripts/**` therefore absorbs `scripts/__tests__/**` and `scripts/lib/__tests__/**` as machinery, while `tests/**`, a declaration tree's own `__tests__/**`, and any `*.test.ts` under `blocks/`/`demos/` count as product. Change this by adding a rule ABOVE the group you want to carve out of.
conventions.generated: Generated and vendored files are `other`, not `product` or `machinery` — nobody authored those lines, so crediting them to either side inflates that week's output. Each generated-file rule names the command that writes it, so the list can be re-checked when a generator moves.
conventions.productScope: WHAT MAKES A PATH `product`. The test is *does this cross the seam?* — is it part of what Web Everything ships to Frontier UI and to any other implementor. Three families qualify and all three are ruled below: (1) the SITE and its spec data (`src/`), the blocks and demos that render it, and their tests; (2) the standard's own DECLARATIONS — the published contract distributions (`contracts/`, `capability-manifest/`, `webcases/`, `validation-generation/`, each a real `@webeverything/*` package with an `exports` map), the capability and conformance substrate (`capabilities/`, `conformance-vectors/`, `conformance-evidence/`, `wrapper-conformance/`), and the 36 per-domain declaration trees. Be precise about the evidence for that third group, because it is the load-bearing one: 31 of the 36 hold a `contract.ts` or `*-contract.ts`, and 17 of the 36 carry the claim that this module is or 'can become the `@webeverything/contracts/<x>` entry (#872/#874) that FUI depends on (the FUI→WE arrow), superseding byte-replication'. That is near-verbatim, not verbatim: the tail from `entry (#872/#874)` onward is identical in all 17, but 14 lead with 'can become the' while three (`webcompliance/`, `webpolicy/`, `webtheme/`) lead with 'is the' — and every one of them carries the `(#872/#874)` citation mid-sentence, so a grep for the sentence without it finds nothing. Seven `blocks/*/contract.ts` files carry the same sentence — six with `(#872/#879)`, and `blocks/dockable/` with `(#872/#874)` — but blocks are ruled by the `blocks/**` rule above and sit OUTSIDE these 36, so they are not counted here. The other 19 do NOT say that, and five of them (`error-summary/`, `interaction-state/`, `module-resolution/`, `source-resolution/`, `webtraits/`) hold no contract file at all — they are dependency-free models and resolvers, ruled `product` on the seam test itself rather than on a self-description, and #1294 (open) argues some WE-resident logic of exactly this kind should relocate to FUI. (3) any file with a declaration SHAPE — `contract.ts`, `*-contract.ts`, `*.vectors.ts` — wherever it lands, so a NEW domain's contract is product from the day it is written rather than the day someone remembers to add a directory rule. What does NOT qualify: anything that only helps us build or ship the above (`scripts/`, `tools/`, `docs/`, `.github/`) — that is machinery — and write-ups about the work (`reports/`, and today `audits/`), which are neither. `eleventy/` and the root `.eleventy.js` are that same build-side kind, but NO rule classifies them, so they fall to `other` rather than to machinery; see `knownGap`.
conventions.default: A path matching no rule falls to `other`. `other` is reported alongside the two headline numbers precisely so the reader can see how much of the tree the classification does NOT cover — a large `other` is a signal that this file needs a new rule, not that the metric is wrong.
conventions.knownGap: READ THIS BEFORE CITING THE PRODUCT NUMBER. The default is NOT symmetric between the two headline classes, and the asymmetry still runs one way, though it is now small. Machinery lives in a stable, fully-covered set of directories (scripts/, backlog/, .claude/, skills-src/, agent-memory-src/, docs/, .github/, .githooks/, tools/), so machinery coverage is effectively complete. Product is covered in the four original homes (src/, blocks/, demos/, tests/) PLUS, since this revision, the standard's own declarations: the four `@webeverything/*` contract packages, the capability/conformance substrate, and the 36 per-domain declaration trees — 44 directories, plus the three declaration-shape rules that catch a new domain's `contract.ts` before anyone writes it a directory rule. EIGHT tracked top-level directories remain unmatched and still fall to `other`: `audits/`, `bun-trial/`, `config/`, `design-refs/`, `design-systems/`, `eleventy/`, `functions/`, `site/`, `test-pages/` — 5,245 tracked TEXT lines at the 2026-08-09 HEAD, down from 26,670 before this revision, and 81 / 0 / 28 / 0 / 0 added lines across the five weeks measured on 2026-08-09 (so closing the rest would move the weekly product figure by at most tens of lines). Unmatched ROOT files (AGENTS.md, package.json, the migration write-ups) add a further 3,522 tracked lines and are deliberately left unruled. The previous revision quoted 38,852 for the old gap; that figure counted newline BYTES in binary assets too (the .webp screenshots under design-refs/, 8,644 such bytes) and does not reproduce as a text-line count. Measured that same crude way the residual here is 17,410 (13,889 in the eight directories + 3,522 root), which reproduces exactly; the old scope measured the same crude way comes to 38,953, so 38,852 is 101 lines off and does not reproduce precisely either. The text-line figures above are the honest ones. Two of those eight are live questions rather than settled `other`: `config/` is not build config at all — `config/resolverContract.ts` says 'WE keeps the interface + vectors; FUI keeps the runtime' — and `design-systems/` describes itself as 'WE-owned data, not scorer code'. Both would be `product` under the test in `productScope`; both are left unruled deliberately, pending an operator call. So the published `product` figure is STILL a LOWER BOUND and the machinery:product ratio still an UPPER bound — just by 5,245 tracked lines rather than 26,670. BUT THE BIAS IS NO LONGER PURELY ONE-WAY, and anyone quoting the number should know it. `src/**` is `product` because the site is a product (the operator's direction), yet `src/_includes/research-descriptions/**` is write-ups ABOUT the delivery loop published as /research/ pages — the same genre `reports/**` is explicitly `other`. It contributed 506 / 808 / 72 / 369 / 0 added lines over the five weeks: 39% of every `product` line in the window, and 42% of the 2026-07-13 week that reads 7.2×. That is more than this whole revision added (404 / 26 / 193 / 0 / 0). Whether a write-up about the loop is still `product` when the product site renders it is an open operator call, and it pushes the figure the OPPOSITE way from the coverage gap above. `KNOWN_UNCOVERED` in the test suite pins that eight-directory list, so a NEW uncovered directory fails loudly instead of silently joining the remainder, and closing any part of the gap forces this paragraph to be rewritten in the same diff.

vendored copy of the plugs runtime that Frontier UI owns (#606); deleted from this tree by #1504, kept as a rule so historical weeks never credit WE with another repo's code
backlog bookkeeping — one markdown card per work item, the tracker itself
delivery machinery — the scripts that run the loop, including their own __tests__ (tests of machinery are machinery)
build and delivery tooling
JSON schemas for the delivery loop's own contracts (the dispatched-worker result object); read by scripts/operations, not shipped as product
agent harness — hooks, commands and settings that drive the loop
agent skills; `.claude/skills` is a symlink to this directory (scripts/sync-skills-deploy.mjs), so this is the same machinery as .claude/ with a different home

the lane transport's own bookkeeping — written by scripts/lane-pool.mjs and dropped again at land (#2288); it was the single largest unclassified contributor before this rule (+1,170 lines over 2026-07-06..2026-08-09)

the rest of docs/ is delivery-side too — design notes and mocks for the agent surfaces (docs/design/**). An earlier revision asserted 'the whole of docs/ is docs/agent/ today', which is true of the HEAD tree but was NOT true of the measured window: +1,033 lines of docs/design/ landed in the week of 2026-07-13 and fell to `other` against that stated intent
CI workflows and issue templates — the delivery pipeline
git hooks that gate the loop

analysis and review write-ups — neither product code nor delivery machinery; stated explicitly rather than left to the default so the choice is visible and arguable. DECLARATION SHAPE, not a directory: a `contract.ts` is by convention this repo's compile-erased pure-contract half — the module that becomes a `@webeverything/contracts/<x>` entry FUI depends on. Stated as a shape so a NEW domain's contract counts as product the day it is written, before anyone adds its directory rule. THE ORDERING ONLY PROTECTS TREES THAT HAVE A RULE: the machinery and `reports/` rules above keep this out of `scripts/`, `tools/`, `docs/`, `backlog/`, `.claude/`, `skills-src/`, `agent-memory-src/`, `.github/`, `.githooks/` and `reports/` — it does NOT protect the eight directories `knownGap` pins as uncovered, so `eleventy/x/contract.ts` or `functions/x.vectors.ts` WOULD score `product` today. That exposure is real but currently empty: no tracked file and no path in the five measured weeks is classified by any shape rule, and the test `a shape rule still reaches into the uncovered directories` pins it so it cannot change unnoticed

the same declaration shape when a domain declares more than one contract in a tree (notifications/push-contract.ts, manifests/changelog-contract.ts, config/resolverContract.ts's camelCase cousin excepted — see knownGap)

a conformance vector suite is a declaration wherever it sits: `<standard>.vectors.ts` exports a `ConformanceVectorSuite` that any implementor's driver runs against its own candidate. The generated `*.vectors.json` is excluded by a rule at the top of this file
